result.title: Compile as Hypothesis: A Headroom Typology for Prompt Optimization on Real Reasoning Models
result.summary: Automated prompt compilers search for or rewrite prompts under the implicit assumption that optimization consistently improves downstream task performance. We evaluate this assumption on frontier reasoning models through rigorous paired, same-day measurements. Across four optimizer families (genome search, profile-guided mutation, GEPA, and ESPO) and eight tasks, structured search yields no statistically significant accuracy gains on strong reasoners. However, a discrete structural genome provides essential architectural stability, preventing catastrophic bimodal seed-collapse (where unconstrained search collapses toward the judge floor in 3/5 runs). Through 190-problem evaluations on knowledge-intensive benchmarks, we establish a three-dimensional headroom typology: prompt optimization cannot compensate for intrinsic knowledge deficits or physical token truncation, but successfully resolves protocol and formatting errors. On gpt-6, while free-text reflective search (GEPA) yields a +.14 gain on a task where structured search remains flat, qualitative ablation reveals that ~.035 stems from judge-rubric reconstruction while ~.105 reflects genuine instruction refinement. Our pre-registered AutoAPC-Select deployment gate matches the oracle policy in 5/7 groups and rescues seed-collapse arms with zero regret. Finally, we expose silent backend-mixing in commercial APIs during outage windows and provide automated per-call audit verification tools to ensure empirical evaluation fidelity.

AI.brief_summary: 论文以同日配对测量在 frontier reasoning models 上检验四类自动 prompt 优化器在八个任务上是否真能提升准确率，提出区分「知识缺陷、token 截断、协议与格式错误」的三维 headroom 分型，并给出预注册的选择门控与商业 API 后端混用审计工具。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 headroom 分型与「judge-rubric 重建 vs 真实指令改进」的增益分解，可能可供核查 LVR 中的性能增益究竟来自 latent 内容还是表面格式与评测伪影；预注册选择门控或可对照停止与答案选择策略，需读原文确认可迁移性。
